target_customer: Frontend and product teams that review work in progress on deployed previews
problem: Reviewers could not easily give feedback on frontend changes in progress. FeaturePeek deployed a preview per branch with an overlay for annotated screenshots, recordings, comments and tickets, with no code changes.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription with an indie CLI tier and a teams tier
product_category: Developer tools, frontend deployment previews and design review

founders.name: Jason Barry
founders.background_notes: Listed on YC page; no background found in sources opened.

founders.name: Eric Silverman
founders.background_notes: Listed on YC page; no background found in sources opened.

technical_complexity.rationale: Branch deployment hosting plus a browser overlay for screenshots and recordings; standard web engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Hosting platforms like Netlify could add the same overlay, which Netlify did after acquiring the team.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Netlify acquired the team and technology on May 19, 2021 and folded the features into Deploy Previews; the standalone product was deprecated on June 18, 2021.

market_need_then: Deploy previews were an established hosting feature; FeaturePeek bet teams needed stronger feedback tooling on top. Netlify said other tools were far less advanced than FeaturePeek's, per TechCrunch.

branding.domain_note: Used featurepeek.com; the domain now serves an unrelated product called PeekFlow, so ownership changed after the sale.

rebrands.why: Product absorbed into Netlify after the acquisition

brand_strength.rationale: Four person team; product launched on Product Hunt in July 2019 but no brand press or community found, and the brand was retired within a month of the 2021 deal.

outcome_analysis: FeaturePeek was a four person YC Summer 2019 team that raised a 1.8M seed led by Matrix Partners in May 2020 and was bought by Netlify on May 19, 2021 for an undisclosed price. The product was folded into Netlify Deploy Previews and the standalone service shut on June 18, 2021, so the outcome was a small team and technology absorption by the platform whose feature it extended, not an independent business.
notes: TechCrunch says FeaturePeek raised about 2M in total versus the 1.8M seed; no other round found, coverage marked complete on the strength of that. Competitor search found no dated 2019 coverage naming rivals (only Netlify and Product Hunt pages and a disputed Heroku Review Apps priority claim), so the list is empty. Founder backgrounds and education not found. Name origin not found. The company's featurepeek.com site now shows an unrelated product called PeekFlow. Netlify's press release describes FeaturePeek as backed by YC and Matrix Partners.
